record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present, though some figures and portions of the extracted text are garbled.
record.tranche_reason: It measures neuron-level linguistic selectivity and compares it with whole-vector probing using a method different from the toy-model superposition method. This bears indirectly on whether LLM representations are localized to individual units, but it does not measure overlapping feature directions or superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition and SAE work as context but reports no results from those studies and does not test feature overlap, feature sparsity, feature importance, or capacity competition. Its own NSI analyses measure selectivity of scalar residual-stream dimensions for grammatical minimal pairs. Targeted ablations test causal reliance, not the listed versions' feature geometry, so they are not included as rows. Raw-score localization results and the probe-versus-behavior comparisons do not directly measure the listed feature geometry and are not extracted as claim rows.
record.test_reason: V4 is tested indirectly with a probe-free method. Across seven LLM checkpoints, single residual-stream units rarely separate grammatical minimal pairs strongly. The whole vector decodes them well (layer-14 probe 0.917), so the authors conclude grammatical information is distributed across many weakly selective units. The study does not test superposition geometry, capacity competition or SAE features.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that permutation-normalized single-unit selectivity is sparse, weak and narrowly tuned, and that strong grammatical 'grandmother neurons' are rare. Grammatical information is linearly decodable from the whole vector without being localized to individual units. Decodability, unit selectivity and behaviour are dissociated, and targeted ablations of high-NSI groups show no effect beyond random controls. The paraphrase should add that the authors explicitly interpret the pattern as distributed encoding.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a probe-free, permutation-normalized minimal-pair neuron selectivity measure and whole-vector probing in trained LLM checkpoints; it does not use toy networks or the original superposition feature-direction analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports robustness across seven checkpoints, NSI thresholds, similarity metrics, and pairing controls. It also reports that random pairing and critical-token deletion affect the measured separability.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-unit tuning breadth is low across 68 contrasts in all seven checkpoints (mean 1.72–2.68 paradigms; P95 5–7; under 1% of units respond to 10 or more). Even poly-selective units keep a dominant within-domain preference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over a fixed set of linguistic contrasts, residual-stream units are narrowly tuned rather than broadly polysemantic. This is a measure of the breadth of unit responses across tested contrasts, not of feature superposition.

record.problems: The evidence concerns seven decoder-only checkpoints and controlled, templated English minimal-pair resources, using last-token scalar dimensions. The paper states that this may miss information at earlier positions or in other components, and that the ablation follow-up covers only three paradigms in one checkpoint and reuses the selection/evaluation pairs.
record.rows_left_out: Raw separability layer-localization results and the full paradigm-level distributions are not extracted because they do not directly establish feature-direction geometry. The targeted ablation results are not included because they test causal behavioral reliance rather than a listed claim version.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
Capacity competition and dedicated dimensions for important features are not tested.
Non-capacity origins of polysemantic units are not tested.
SAE-recoverable sparse features are not tested. Only 68 English minimal-pair contrasts at the last-token residual stream are examined, and no specific feature direction is identified.
All of it: no SAEs are trained or evaluated.
All of it: feature dimensionality is not examined.

missing.what: Number of paradigms with any NSI>2 unit for each checkpoint (2–6) and NSI>2 unit fractions (about 1e-4 to 2e-3 %), i.e. the cross-model counterpart of R5

Threshold sweep: at NSI>1 only 0.094% of units (mean 27 per paradigm) pass; from 1.645 to 3 only 3/68 paradigms have any unit. Under Spearman and cosine variants, more than 99.7% of units stay below z>2.

Targeted ablation of top-NSI groups (k=5/10/20) is no more damaging than 100 random same-layer sets (all p≥0.109; accuracy change ≤0.009). The authors read this as consistent with distributed or redundant encoding.
Layer-14 probe accuracy is negatively correlated with mean NSI across paradigms (r=-0.557)

record.verdict_notes: The 'neurons' here are residual-stream coordinates, not MLP neurons. That basis is not privileged, which weakens the link between unit-level selectivity and superposition claims; a researcher should weigh this. The authors cite Toy Models of Superposition only as context, and mention superposition as one possible explanation for the null ablation results. The reader's limits_scope label (based on R23-R24) is dropped: those are validation controls, and the interpretive caveat belongs under untested parts.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-count-to-dimension ratio, overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry are tested.
The paper measures tuning breadth as a proxy for polysemanticity but does not test capacity competition, feature importance, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
The study does not test alternative causal origins of polysemantic neurons.

Tests neuron-level selectivity for English minimal-pair linguistic contrasts, not the distribution of general model features or SAE-recoverable features. It does not identify feature directions or establish that an individual feature is distributed across neurons.
No SAE features are extracted or evaluated for completeness, stability, canonical status, or behavioral relevance.
Treats scalar dimensions as units for its measurement but does not establish whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: English minimal-pair linguistic contrasts in the seven tested checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: The study reports sparse positive unit selectivity and rare strongly selective units, alongside high whole-vector probe accuracy, consistent with information not being strongly localized to individual units (R1-R22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Interpretation of unit-level NSI as evidence about feature distribution
reader_labels.reason: NSI measures scalar-unit selectivity for these contrasts and does not locate feature directions or show that a particular feature is spread across units; same-label pairing controls also show that raw separability alone can arise without the targeted contrast (R23-R24).
